strategy.summary: Reproduce the f8 layout-conversion MLIR error in Mosaic GPU by building jaxlib from source at the buggy revision (32ea97614e82), applying the developer's test_fp8_relayout, and running it on a Blackwell-class CUDA GPU with wg semantics disabled. On the buggy revision the test should error during compilation with an MLIR error from reconcile-unrealized-casts and unresolved casts. On the fixed revision it should pass with exact equality.

pip_packages: jax (source checkout, unpinned: no documented constraint)
jaxlib (built from source at the buggy revision, unpinned: no documented constraint)
system_packages: CUDA toolkit and driver with a GPU that supports the tcgen05/TMEM layouts used by the test (Blackwell-class, sm_100 or newer; inferred from TCGEN05_TMEM_NATIVE, not stated as a requirement in the evidence)
clang or gcc and bazel as required by the jaxlib build
build_commands: git checkout 32ea97614e82 (buggy revision; the fix is its child)
git apply the developer test diff to tests/pallas/mosaic_gpu_test.py
python build/build.py --enable_cuda (flags for Mosaic GPU/CUDA plugin per the repo's build docs; exact flags not in evidence)
pip install dist/jaxlib-*.whl and pip install -e . for jax
export JAX_PLATFORMS=cuda or ensure a CUDA backend is visible
pinned_because: No documented version constraint for jax or jaxlib exists in the evidence; the era constraint is only the PR date 2026-01-29, so the source checkout at the buggy commit is used as the version and nothing else is pinned.

strategy.reproducing_test: tests/pallas/mosaic_gpu_test.py::MosaicGpuTest::test_fp8_relayout (parameterized over from_narrow False and True; class name inferred from file context, verify against the file)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 32ea97614e82 with the test applied, both parameterizations raise an MLIR error during layout conversion (reconcile-unrealized-casts leaves UnrealizedConversionCastOp that cannot cancel for f8 values), so the test fails. On the fixed revision (child commit), both parameterizations compile and run, and np.testing.assert_array_equal(kernel(x), x) passes with exact equality, so the test passes. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Not needed: the failure is a compile-time exception, not a wrong value. If the MLIR error does not reproduce, check that the pass pipeline in jaxlib/mosaic/gpu/custom_call.cc still runs reconcile-unrealized-casts before mosaic-convert-gpu-to-llvm.

input_output_examples.input: test_fp8_relayout, shape (128, 32), dtype jnp.float8_e4m3fn, from_narrow in {False, True}, x = jax.random.normal(jax.random.key(10), shape).astype(float8_e4m3fn)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: MLIR error during layout conversion (exact message not given in evidence)
input_output_examples.expected_output: no MLIR error; kernel(x) equals x under np.testing.assert_array_equal (exact equality)

risks: The defect only appears on a GPU that supports the TCGEN05_TMEM_NATIVE layouts; on other architectures the test may skip or fail for unrelated reasons, so it will not transition there. The sm level is inferred, not stated in the evidence.
Bugs in the Mosaic GPU path are sensitive to the CUDA toolkit and LLVM/MLIR version bundled in the bazel build; a mismatched toolchain may produce a different error or none.
The test is skipped under wg semantics (skip_if_wg_semantics). Do not set the wg semantics mode or the test will skip and show no transition.
Pass ordering matters: if the pipeline is reordered again, the MLIR error may return on the fixed revision, so verify the order in custom_call.cc.
The exact MLIR error text is not in the evidence, so match on the failure type and the test's error state, not on a specific string.
No jax or jaxlib version is documented, so the source checkout at the buggy commit is the only pin; a wheel from PyPI will not reproduce the bug.

oracle.reference_source: the input x itself, in tests/pallas/mosaic_gpu_test.py test_fp8_relayout
oracle.why: The test compares kernel(x) to x with np.testing.assert_array_equal, so any round-trip rounding error would fail it. The bug is an exception, though, so the oracle matters mainly on the fixed revision.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Compilation of the kernel raises an MLIR error during layout conversion because f8 values are not representable in LLVM IR and the UnrealizedConversionCastOps do not cancel. The exception propagates out of kernel(x), so the test errors before the assertion runs.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The f8 source is bitcast through UnrealizedConversionCastOp to an integer vector of the same width and cast back, and the pass reorder lets the casts cancel. The kernel compiles and returns x exactly, so assert_array_equal passes for both from_narrow values.
